module.purpose: Provides a React hook that tracks whether configured keyboard keys or key combinations are currently pressed.
module.summary: This module parses individual keys and combinations, selects event.key or event.code based on the requested values, and maintains pressed-key state through keyboard and browser lifecycle events. It supports configurable event targets, input-field behavior, default prevention, modifier keys, alternative combinations, and reset handling for blur, context-menu, and macOS Command-key behavior.
module.businessContext: Supports keyboard shortcuts and interaction controls in the React product UI. Failure prevents reliable shortcut activation or leaves pressed-state indicators stale.

units.name: useKeyPress

detail.name: useKeyPress
detail.signature: export function useKeyPress(keyCode: KeyCode | null = null, options: UseKeyPressOptions = { target: defaultDoc, actInsideInputWithModifier: true }): boolean
preconditions: The hook is invoked within a React render context.
When keyCode is non-null, the configured target and window must support keyboard and lifecycle event listener registration.
postconditions: Returns a boolean indicating whether the configured key input is currently matched.
When keyCode is null, no configured key is tracked and the returned state remains false.
Matching keydown events set the returned state to true.
Matching keyup events, window blur, and contextmenu events reset the returned state to false.
invariants: Pressed keys are tracked as a set, so repeated keydown events do not create duplicate entries.
A key combination matches only when the currently pressed keys satisfy one of the configured key combinations.
Event listeners are removed when the effect is cleaned up or its dependencies change.
Modifier state is cleared after keyup handling.
edgeCases: A string keyCode represents one key or a '+'-delimited combination.
An array keyCode represents multiple alternative keys or combinations.
A keyCode containing '++' preserves '+' as a key within the parsed combination.
Keyboard events from input-like DOM nodes are ignored when no modifier is pressed, and are also ignored with a modifier when actInsideInputWithModifier is false.
For matching keydown events, default prevention is skipped for interactive BUTTON or A targets unless a modifier key is pressed; otherwise preventDefault is applied when preventDefault is not false.
A Meta keyup or a window blur/contextmenu event clears all tracked pressed keys.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Non-string entries in an array keyCode are filtered out; a null keyCode disables key tracking. No explicit exception or fallback error is produced.

stateMutations: React state tracking whether the configured key input is pressed.
Mutable pressed-key set used to track currently held keys.
Mutable modifier-key flag used during keyboard event handling.
Keyboard and window event listener registrations on the configured target and window.

units.name: isMatchingKey

detail.name: isMatchingKey
detail.signature: function isMatchingKey(keyCodes: Array<Keys>, pressedKeys: PressedKeys, isUp: boolean): boolean
preconditions: keyCodes is an array of key combinations.
pressedKeys represents the currently pressed keys.
isUp is a boolean indicating whether the comparison is for key release.
postconditions: Returns a boolean indicating whether a configured key combination matches the pressed keys.
When isUp is false, only key combinations whose length equals pressedKeys.size are considered.
invariants: The input collections are not mutated.
For key-up comparisons, key-combination length is not filtered by pressedKeys.size.
For key-down comparisons, combinations with a different number of keys from pressedKeys.size are excluded before matching.
edgeCases: When isUp is false and a configured key combination has a different length from pressedKeys.size, that combination is ignored.
When isUp is true, configured key combinations are not excluded based on their length.
Multiple configured key combinations are evaluated as alternatives.
detail.summary: Determines whether the currently pressed keys match at least one configured key combination, with key-count filtering applied for key-down matching.
